Subject: Private CP authn/authz path mapping + network boundary access inventory

Hi Michael / BrightBank ops team,

Following up from last week's discovery call — we're preparing the operator-access and SCIM/SAML handoff for BrightBank's private control plane. To make the cutover deterministic we need a short inventory and a mapping matrix from your side. Can you provide the items below by EOD Monday so we can finalize the runbook?

Requested deliverables (concise):
- Network boundary inventory: IP ranges, NAT/gateway addresses, and exact ports you can open to our control plane (preferred CIDR format).
- Jumpbox access pattern: Do you plan to use a customer-managed bastion, or will Redwood operate a managed jumpbox within your VPC? If customer-managed, provide SSH key handling and expiry policy.
- SAML metadata: IdP metadata XML, single-sign-on URL, and attribute mappings for email, groups, and a role claim.
- SCIM provisioning: preferred SCIM base URL, auth method (bearer / mTLS), and a sample provisioning payload or group mapping doc.
- Operator accounts: list of operator identities that need delegated admin (email + role), and requested audit log retention for actions (we default to 90 days).

Attachment stubs: feel free to attach a compact CSV or small JSON sample. We will use these to generate the private CP operator role bindings and firewall change request.

I'll consolidate and produce a proposed access plan (including short-lived cert suggestion) for review. If you prefer a 30-min walkthrough instead of the inventory post, tell us preferred times — we can be flexible.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the initial inventory and a SCIM sample. Quick notes below and answers inline.

- Network boundary inventory: attached brightbank-firewall-inventory.csv (internal CIDRs removed for thread) — public egress to your control plane allowed from 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/28 via our NATs. Ports we can commit to opening: 443 (HTTPS), 8443 (alternate), 22 to our bastion only.
- Jumpbox: we will operate a customer-managed bastion (bastion-1.brightbank.internal). SSH keys are managed via our internal KMS and rotated every 30 days; we can add Redwood's ephemeral cert CA for short-lived certs if you prefer.
- SAML: IdP metadata XML attached (scoped). Attribute mapping: email->mail, groups->memberOf, roleClaim->eduPersonEntitlement. We can add a custom attribute if needed.
- SCIM: sample attached brightbank-scim-sample.json. We'll use bearer tokens scoped to SCIM provisioning. Token rotation window is 60 days.
- Operators: provisional operator list in the CSV; retention: we can accept 180 days of audit exports to an S3 bucket you provide, or we can work with your archive pipeline.

We also flagged two constraints:
1) We cannot expose internal admin endpoints over the public internet; we'll need an IP-restricted peering/site-to-site or a customer-managed VPN for the control plane management interface.
2) HSM/KMS: Keys are managed via our AWS KMS (multi-account). We need to confirm your support for customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest of operator credentials.

Attaching: brightbank-firewall-inventory.csv, brightbank-scim-sample.json, brightbank-saml-metadata.xml.

—Michael

Subject: Re: Private CP authn/authz path mapping + network boundary access inventory

Thanks Michael — very helpful. A few follow-ups / concerns from the operator and security side:

1) VPN vs peering: If BrightBank cannot expose the admin endpoints publicly, we need to choose between a site-to-site VPN or a VPC peering + routing policy. Peering is lower latency but requires route table coordination and cross-account IR; VPN is easier but we need to validate MTU and path MT. Which do you recommend ops?

2) Short-lived operator creds: We should prefer short-lived certs issued by Redwood's operator CA that chain to a customer-trusted root. Michael mentioned adding our ephemeral cert CA — request: provide the CA bundle and an expiration policy for the keys we sign. We will not accept long-lived static SSH keys for operator accounts.

3) SCIM group->role mapping: sample mappings (proposed): SCIM group "rl-priv-admins" -> Redwood role: PRIV_CP_ADMIN; "rl-operators" -> OPERATOR_READWRITE. We need BrightBank to confirm exact group names or provide a mapping table. Also confirm whether you want dynamic role revocation delay (i.e., effective immediately or X minutes).

4) KMS/HSM integration: We will support customer-managed keys for encrypting operator secrets, but need an IAM role in BrightBank that allows Redwood to PutObject to a dedicated S3 staging bucket for audit exports and a key policy statement in your KMS that allows our service account to encrypt/decrypt. Can you partner on a draft policy?

5) Audit sync cadence: propose daily push of audit bundle to S3 and a weekly signed digest for compliance. Is 24h push acceptable?

If ops prefers, we can run a 30-min technical call to walk through the SCIM payload, SAML attributes, and the firewall changes. I can lead the runbook authoring once these items are confirmed.

Marissa Cole
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Private CP authn/authz path mapping + network boundary access inventory

Marissa / team — quick answers inline:

1) Peering vs VPN: we recommend peering for consistent management-plane latency. We can set up a dedicated peering connection scoped to the control-plane subnets. We'll coordinate route tables and will need the exact CIDRs your control plane will advertise.

2) Short-lived certs: we can accept Redwood-signed ephemeral certs. We'll provide a CA trust bundle; rotation policy: CA cert rotation annually, ephemeral cert TTL 4 hours.

3) SCIM mappings: we'll confirm group names by EOD — current group names are rl_privadmins and rl_operators (underscore variant). We prefer immediate revocation semantics.

4) KMS policy: attaching a draft KMS policy snippet in the shared drive (DOCID-4521). We can authorize a cross-account IAM role that allows Get/Decrypt on the CMK and S3 PutObject on the audit bucket.

5) Audit sync: 24h push OK — we also support near-real-time via SNS if you prefer future improvements.

I'll be available Friday 10-11am PT for a quick run-through.

—Michael
